catalyst_text: Initiated Phase 2 study in Down syndrome Alzheimers
detailed_catalyst_text: Initiation of a Phase 2 study in people with Down syndrome–associated Alzheimer’s disease was announced, with a poster detailing the design and rationale. This marks progression of an APP‑lowering RNAi approach into mid‑stage testing in a genetically defined AD population.
catalyst_text_evidence: The company announced the initiation of a Phase 2 study of mivelsiran in people with Down syndrome-associated AD and presented a poster detailing the design and rationale. The APPlauDS Study (evaluating APP-lowering to reduce amyloid accumulation in Down syndrome) will be recruiting people with Down syndrome with early-stage AD across approximately 30 global sites.

catalyst_text: Updated Phase 1 results showed positive safety biomarkers
detailed_catalyst_text: Updated Phase 1 data in early-onset Alzheimer’s disease showed no evidence of increased ARIA risk and robust, durable reductions in CSF sAPPβ and Aβ42 with up to 30 months of exposure. Adverse events were mostly procedural pain and headache, with no serious or severe events deemed related.
catalyst_text_evidence: An additional presentation included updated data from the Phase 1 trial of mivelsiran in patients with early-onset Alzheimer’s disease. An analysis of safety data from single- and multiple-doses of mivelsiran showed no evidence of increased risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormality (ARIA) events. Results also showed robust, durable reductions in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) soluble amyloid beta precursor protein (sAPPβ) and amyloid beta 42 (Aβ42), with up to 30 months of treatment exposure. The most common adverse events (AEs) were procedural pain and procedural headache, and no serious or severe AEs were deemed related to study drug.

catalyst_text: Completed enrollment initial results expected in 2028
detailed_catalyst_text: Enrollment has been completed in the Phase 2 cAPPricorn-1 study in cerebral amyloid angiopathy. The primary endpoint is the rate of new lobar microbleeds by MRI, positioning the study for an initial results readout in 2028.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alnylam also announced today that it has completed enrollment in the Phase 2 cAPPricorn-1 study of mivelsiran in CAA, a leading cause of hemorrhagic stroke. cAPPricorn-1’s primary endpoint is rate of new lobar microbleeds measured by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with initial results expected in 2028.

catalyst_text: Presented preclinical data and Phase 1 trial design
detailed_catalyst_text: Presentations highlighted preclinical data and the design of the ongoing first-in-human Phase 1 study in Alzheimer’s patients. The trial initiated in Q4 2025, advancing a tau-targeting RNAi therapeutic into clinical development.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alnylam also highlighted progress with ALN-5288 – an investigational asset in development in collaboration with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals – in presentations of preclinical data and of the design of the ongoing first-in-human Phase 1 trial (NCT07214727), which initiated in the fourth quarter of 2025.

catalyst_text: Presented pooled safety data showing no ocular concerns
detailed_catalyst_text: A pooled assessment across clinical trials and post-marketing use in transthyretin amyloidosis examined vitamin A deficiency-related safety with RNAi therapies. Findings across more than 25,000 patient-years showed low, placebo-comparable ocular event rates and no clinically meaningful deficiency.
catalyst_text_evidence: A separate pooled analysis of clinical trial and post-marketing safety data evaluated the relationship between transthyretin-lowering RNAi therapies and vitamin A deficiency-related adverse events. The analysis included more than 25,000 patient-years of treatment exposure across vutrisiran and patisiran programs. Rates of ocular adverse events potentially associated with vitamin A deficiency were low and comparable to placebo. No cases of clinically meaningful vitamin A deficiency were observed.

catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 3 results across clinical subgroups
detailed_catalyst_text: New subgroup analyses from the HELIOS-B Phase 3 study in cardiomyopathy due to transthyretin amyloidosis were presented, showing reduced all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular events versus placebo. Benefits were maintained across high-risk subgroups and with background therapies, supporting consistent efficacy in real-world-like patients.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ... today announced new analyses from the HELIOS-B Phase 3 study of vutrisiran in patients with the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM).... The data presented at Heart Failure 2026, the annual congress of the Heart Failure Association of the European Society of Cardiology, show consistent clinical benefit across patient populations commonly encountered in clinical practice.... In patients with atrial fibrillation, representing approximately 65% of the HELIOS-B study population and associated with more advanced disease, vutrisiran significantly reduced the risk of all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular (CV) events compared with placebo. Treatment effects were also maintained in patients with low systolic blood pressure (SBP), a higher-risk phenotype, with vutrisiran slowing the progressive decline in SBP observed over time.

catalyst_text: Presented supportive pooled Phase 2 safety data hypertension
detailed_catalyst_text: Pooled safety results from the Phase 2 KARDIA program were presented, showing an acceptable safety profile in patients with hypertension, including those at high cardiovascular risk or with lower eGFR. Clinically relevant events such as hypotension, hyperkalemia, and eGFR decline were low and largely transient, including when combined with ACE inhibitors or ARBs, supporting continued late-stage evaluation.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alnylam also presented pooled Phase 2 safety data for zilebesiran, an investigational RNAi therapeutic being evaluated for cardiovascular risk reduction in patients with hypertension, with the potential to provide continuous control of blood pressure. A comprehensive analysis of safety across the Phase 2 KARDIA program demonstrated an acceptable safety profile for zilebesiran, both as monotherapy and in combination with standard-of-care antihypertensives, across patients with mild-to-moderate hypertension, those at high CV risk, or with lower eGFR at baseline. In the analysis, clinically relevant safety events, such as hypotension, hyperkalemia, and eGFR decline, were low across the patient populations, including those receiving zilebesiran in combination with an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi) or an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB).

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 data in ATTR cardiomyopathy
detailed_catalyst_text: New analyses from the Phase 3 HELIOS-B study were presented, showing improvements in health-related quality of life and consistent cardiovascular benefits across subgroups, including advanced disease and diastolic dysfunction, in adults with ATTR-CM. A real-world cohort also showed high adherence with quarterly healthcare professional–administered dosing. These results reinforce durable clinical and quality-of-life benefits for this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:ALNY), the leading RNAi therapeutics company, today announced new clinical and real-world data from its cardiovascular (CV) portfolio presented at the American College of Cardiology's Annual Scientific Session and Expo (ACC.26), reinforcing the potential of RNAi to deliver fundamentally differentiated, effective, and durable impact for patients living with cardiovascular disease (CVD). New data continue to support the use of vutrisiran – the first and only transthyretin (TTR) silencer that delivers rapid knockdown of TTR at the source – as a first-line treatment for patients with the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR‑CM). The HELIOS-B analyses demonstrate that vutrisiran delivered meaningful improvements in how patients with ATTR-CM feel and function, with benefits sustained across disease severity, reinforcing how TTR silencing at its source translates into durable clinical and health-related quality-of-life (QoL) benefits for patients. This analysis evaluated placebo-corrected mean score changes of vutrisiran-treated patients across the 23-item Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary Score (KCCQ-OSS) from baseline to 30 Months. Compared to placebo, vutrisiran demonstrated improvements in nearly all components, most notably in physical limitations and QoL. A retrospective cohort study of real-world data in patients with amyloidosis indicated high adherence and persistence to vutrisiran treatment, with most patients still receiving treatment after 12 months. Over the treatment period, 93.8% were adherent to vutrisiran, defined as PDC (proportion of days covered) ≥0.8.
